checks.primaryClaim: ED claims 1-2 days: 'Where the papers are correct, processing takes hardly one to two days, reflecting the newly online process and currently low application volume; no statutory timeline has been notified.' The ED itself flags as MISSING: 'No statutory or public-service guarantee timeline has been notified for Factory License processing.'
checks.sourceSays: The only Nagaland instrument found that states a number of days for a factory licence is the draft State rules under the OSH Code, published in the official Gazette: rule 101(7) - 'A registration certificate for a factory shall be granted in Form-XXIII by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator, or any other officer appointed and specially empowered in this behalf by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator, if the application is complete in all respects but not later than seven days from the date of submission of complete application, failing which such license shall be deemed to have been issued and the license shall be auto generated.' Rule 4(5) says the same for registration of an establishment: 'The certificate of registration shall be issued in Form-II physically/electronically immediately, if the application is complete in all respect, but not later than seven days from the date of submission of complete application'. This is a DRAFT ('Notice is hereby given that the said draft will be taken into consideration after the expiry of a period of thirty (30) days from the date of publication of this Notification in the Official Gazette'), so it is not yet in force. The in-force departmental procedure document 'Registration and Renewal under Factories Act, 1948' prescribes NO processing deadline at all - the only day-figure in it is for renewal filing ('shall be submitted not less than 30 days before the date on which the license expires'). The ED's 1-2 day figure is therefore not contradicted (it sits inside the proposed 7-day outer limit) but no official source states or corroborates it.

checks.primaryClaim: ED: 'Fee varies according to the number of employees and the horsepower utilized. A fee chart exists in the portal but the expert did not provide the actual amounts. Payment is made only after final approval, after which the applicant downloads the certificate.' ED gap flagged MISSING: 'Exact Factory License fee amounts are not available'.
checks.sourceSays: The Labour & Employment Department's own fee notification supplies the amounts the ED could not. Notification NO. LAB - 1/24/2000, dated Kohima the 15th June 2000: 'In partial modification of this Department Notification of even No. L&E - 1/4/86 dated. 29th September, 1989 and in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 6 of the Factories Act, 1948, the Governor of Nagaland hereby revises the rates payable for registration and renewal of factories as appended in Schedule - I in the state of Nagaland with effect from the date of issue of this Notification.' Its annexure is headed 'SCHEDULE - 01 / SCALE OF FEES PAYABLE FOR REGISTRATION AND RENEWAL OF FACTORY LICENSES IN THE STATE OF NAGALAND', a matrix of 'Total maximum power installed in H.P.' (rows: Nil, Up to 05, Up to 15, Up to 50, Up to 100, Up to 250, Up to 500, Up to 1,000, Up to 2,000, Up to 5,000, Above 5001) against 'Maximum number of persons to be employed on any one day during the year' (columns: Up to 5, 6 to 15, 16 to 50, 51 to 100, 101 to 250, 251 to 500, 501 to 750, 751 to 1,000, 1,001 to 2,000, Above 2000), '(Fees payable in Rupees)'. The lowest cell is Rs. 120 (Nil H.P. / up to 5 persons) and the highest is Rs. 28,000 (Above 5001 H.P. / above 2000 persons); e.g. Up to 50 H.P. with 16 to 50 persons = Rs. 1,500. This exactly confirms the ED's stated basis (number of employees x horsepower) and supplies the figures. It also shows no percentage-based or gateway-linked charge of the kind the expert speculated about (~5%).

checks.primaryClaim: ED: 'There is no deemed approval for Factory License as of the interview.' (deemedApproval.status = 'no', days = null)
checks.sourceSays: The Labour Department's own in-force process document for the Factories Act contains an express deeming provision at the renewal stage: 'An application for the renewal of license for a period not exceeding 3(three) years shall be made in Form 3 accompanied by a treasury receipt, and shall be submitted not less than 30 days before the date on which the license expires. If the application, complete in all respects, is so made, the premises shall be held to be duly licensed until such date as the Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspector of Factories or the Inspector of Factories renews the license.' Separately, the draft State rules gazetted on 4 June 2026 would create an explicit deemed grant with auto-generation for fresh licences: 'if the application is complete in all respects but not later than seven days from the date of submission of complete application, failing which such license shall be deemed to have been issued and the license shall be auto generated' (rule 101(7)). SCOPE NOTE, so a reviewer is not misled: the in-force provision is a deemed continuation of licensed status pending a renewal decision, not a deemed grant of a first-time licence; the 7-day deemed grant exists only in a draft that is not yet in force. The ED's blanket statement that no deemed approval exists for this service is nevertheless wrong as to the renewal limb.

checks.primaryClaim: ED lists three documents only: 'Plant layout of the factory', 'GPS location of the factory', 'Identity proof of the occupier or manager', adding that 'PAN and Aadhaar are not insisted upon for Factory License' and that 'A checklist is available in the portal'.
checks.sourceSays: The department's published checklist is materially longer and different. For the licence stage: 'List documents required for registration and licencing of factory. 1. Form No.2  2. Certificate of Stability duly signed by the Chartered Engineer/Chartered Architect.  3. Treasury challan for deposit of registration fee for the factory in the Government treasury under the head of account "L&E-0230- in favour of Chief Inspector.  4. Copy of power sanction certificate from concerned authorities.' That stage is reachable only after a separate prior stage whose checklist has sixteen items: '1. Form No-1. 2. Flow-chart of manufacturing process. 3. List of machinery. 4. Site Plan of the factory. 5. Building drawings including elevations, Plans & cross sections. 6. Machine lay out. 7. Latest/ valid copy of NOC from Nagaland Pollution Control Board 8. Latest/ valid copy of NOC from Chief Fire Officer Nagaland regarding fire safety. ... 10. Resolution passed by Board of Directors in which one of the Directors has been declared as occupier ... 12. Memorandum and Articles of Association in case of company. ... 15. Copy of Jamabandi of the site on which the factory is situated...', with the note 'All the drawings are required to be signed by the occupier as well as Chartered Engineer/Chartered Architect.' Nothing in the official checklist asks for a 'GPS location', and no identity document of the occupier/manager is listed as such at the licence stage (Form 2 instead requires the occupier's and manager's full names and residential addresses). Two third-party clearances the ED does not mention - Pollution Control Board NOC and Fire Service NOC - are mandatory at the plan-approval stage.

checks.primaryClaim: ED describes a single five-step online journey: (1) apply online on the Labour Department portal, (2) 'Inspector verifies the application' with 'Inspection may be required for a big establishment; otherwise a physical visit is generally not required', (3) 'Inspector obtains approval from District Officer/Assistant Labour Commissioner (ALC)', (4) factory registered/licensed through the portal 'Once ALC gives approval', (5) 'Applicant pays fee and downloads licence certificate'. automationLevel 'full', applicantOfficeVisit 'no'.
checks.sourceSays: The department's published 'Flow Chart for Registration of Factories' shows TWO sequential applications, not one: 'Factory Owner -> Application for approval of plan and Permission to Construct/extend/or takes into use any building as a factory -> Scrutiny -> Permission to Construct/extend/or takes into use any building as a factory -> Application for registration and grant of license -> Scrutiny -> Grant of license -> Renewal of License', with 'Rectification' loops off each scrutiny. The prior stage is mandatory: 'No site shall be used for the location of a factory or no building in a factory should be constructed, reconstructed, extended or taken into use as a factory or part of a factory unless previous permission in writing is obtained from the Chief Inspector of Factories.' Two further points differ from the ED: (a) the licence is granted by the Chief Inspector, not by the ALC/District Officer - 'A license for a factory shall be granted for a period not exceeding three years by The Chief Inspector in Form 4'; (b) the fee is payable WITH the application, not after approval - the 'Treasury challan for deposit of registration fee' is item 3 of the documents required for licensing, and Form No. 2 column 10 reads 'Amount of fee Rs........ paid into the ......... Treasury/Bank on .......... vide Challan/D.D/Cheque No. ......... (enclosed)'. The ED's inspection point is, separately, broadly supported: the department's published 'COMPLIANCE INSPECTION UNDER THE FACTORIES ACT, 1948' procedure is trigger-based rather than routine - 'Base on the Complain received, accident happens, non compliance to the Act or risk involved etc a factory is identified to carry out an inspection' - and describes no pre-licensing site inspection.

remarks: TRANSPORT NOTE (important for reproducibility): labour.nagaland.gov.in and eodb*.nagaland.gov.in serve a valid Sectigo certificate for *.nagaland.gov.in but OMIT the intermediate, so a default curl fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' - which is why the earlier source-list pass excluded them. This session fixed the chain legitimately, without weakening verification: the leaf's own Authority Information Access extension names http://crt.sectigo.com/SectigoPublicServerAuthenticationCADVR36.crt, that intermediate was downloaded from Sectigo and appended to the session CA bundle, and all fetches below were then made with full TLS verification over https. The four most load-bearing sources in this file come from those previously unreachable hosts.

The three documents cited from labour.nagaland.gov.in are not reachable by a plain GET URL. The Notifications and Informations pages serve each PDF through a POST form (csrfmiddlewaretoken + a hidden numeric id + a 'download' button) targeting the same page URL. The cited URLs are the exact pages fetched; the id values are given in each citation title so a reviewer can reproduce the download. Item ids used: notification id=7 (Factories Act 'Registration Fee Structure' = Notification LAB-1/24/2000); information id=12 ('Registration and Renewal under Factories Act, 1948'); information id=32 ('The Draft Nagaland Code on OSH and WC Rules 2026'); information id=11 ('COMPLIANCE INSPECTION UNDER THE FACTORIES ACT') was also read.

On the headline 1-2 day claim: it could not be confirmed or contradicted by any official source, and nothing currently in force in Nagaland sets any processing deadline for a Factory License. What the record does show is a plausible explanation for why so short a figure is reported - the ED appears to be describing only the final licence-grant step of a two-stage statutory process whose heavy lifting (plan approval, Pollution Control Board NOC, Fire NOC, certificate of stability from a chartered engineer) sits in a separate prior permission stage the ED does not mention at all. Any dashboard figure of 1-2 days for Nagaland should be footnoted accordingly rather than compared head-to-head with states whose timeline covers the whole journey.

Volume corroboration for the ED's 'low application volume' rationale: the Labour Department's live EoDB portal homepage (https://eodblabour.nagaland.gov.in/) displays counters reading 'Public Factories 3', 'Private Factories 4', 'Shops & Establishments 1432', 'Commercial Establishment 94', 'Public Entertainment 1'. Seven registered factories statewide makes a 1-2 day turnaround credible operationally, and is consistent with the ED's statement that Nagaland has no hazardous or big/mega establishments.

Currency caveat on fees: the fee schedule quoted is Notification LAB-1/24/2000 of 15 June 2000, still published by the department as its current Factories Act fee structure, but 26 years old. The draft OSH Code rules gazetted 4 June 2026 propose a replacement schedule for factory licences running from Rs. 390 (Nil H.P. / 20 persons) to Rs. 44,500 (5000+ H.P. / 5000+ persons), and a separate establishment-registration fee scale of Rs. 1,000 (up to 20 employees) to Rs. 20,000 (1001 and above). If and when those rules are finalised, both the fee amounts and the 7-day/deemed-approval timeline in this file change.

Status of the draft rules: 'THE DRAFT NAGALAND CODE ON OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY, HEALTH AND WORKING CONDITIONS RULES, 2026' was published in The Nagaland Gazette Extraordinary No. 20 dated Thursday, June 4, 2026, for a 30-day objection period under sections 133(1) and 135(1) of the OSH Code, 2020. The Nagaland eGazette listing (https://govtpress.nagaland.gov.in/egazette-latest/) was fetched and is live through October 2026, but no subsequent issue confirming final notification of these rules was located, so they must be treated as draft.

The ED's claim that PAN and Aadhaar are not insisted upon is consistent with the in-force checklist (neither appears). However the draft OSH rules would change this: rule 4(3) provides that 'The Permanent Account Number (PAN) or Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number (TAN) of the applicant or the establishment ... may be verified online.'

Issuing authority: DGFASLI's national directory ('List of Chief Inspectors of Factories / Director Industrial Safety and Health, As on 05.06.2024') lists for Nagaland the 'Labour Commissioner & Chief Inspector of Factories & Boilers, Nagaland, Kohima-797 001'. Both that directory and the department's own process note put the licensing power in the Chief Inspector of Factories, which sits uneasily with the ED's step 3 ('Inspector obtains approval from District Officer/Assistant Labour Commissioner'). A 2022 DIPR press release (https://ipr.nagaland.gov.in/node/8001) likewise directs unlicensed units to 'obtain the necessary permits from the Chief Inspector of Factories, Govt. of Nagaland', with penalties of 'imprisonment of up to 6 (six) months or a fine amounting to Rs. 50,000/-'.

Single-window status: the ED states there is 'no inter-departmental coordination and no State Single Window integration for Factory License'. The Labour Department's own factory/shop portal is nonetheless branded 'Ease Of Doing Business / Single Window Clearance System' (https://eodblabour.nagaland.gov.in/), i.e. a departmental single window rather than a State-wide one. NTIIP 2025 (fetched) commits only prospectively, at objective 15, to 'Develop a Single Window Clearance System (SWCS) which will facilitate necessary approvals, clearances, registrations and licenses to the investors and expedite the process of legislating a Public Service Delivery Guarantee Act (PSDGA)'. NTIIP 2025 otherwise contains no Factory License process detail - it lists 'Factory License' only as one of the 'Other Registration / Permission / License / NOC etc. required for establishing and running of the unit'.

Sources fetched that yielded nothing usable: https://eodb.nagaland.gov.in/notifications returned HTTP 200 but is a JavaScript-only shell ('This website requires JavaScript to be enabled'); https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/18999/1/factories_act_1948.pdf returned HTTP 504 on four attempts; https://labour.gov.in/sites/default/files/draftfactory.pdf returned 404; the Assam mirror of the central Act reset the connection. No fetched copy of the central Factories Act, 1948 was therefore obtained, so no check in this file relies on the central Act's own text (e.g. the section 6(2) three-month deeming rule is NOT cited here, because it could not be verified against a fetched source this session).

The in-force departmental process note references rule numbers (Form No. 1 'Prescribed under Rule 3'; Form No. 2 'See Rule 4(1), 7(2) and 12'; Form 3 'See rules 5, 8 and 11'), which indicates the department is administering a set of Factories Rules in practice. No gazette notification of 'Nagaland Factories Rules' was located this session, so the source of those rule numbers remains unverified.
